merger_description:
TurOSI Pty Ltd (**TurOSI**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Cordina Food Group (HoldCo) Pty Ltd (**Cordina**) (the **Acquisition**).

TurOSI is a food manufacturer and chicken meat processor. TurOSI is the Australian subsidiary of the global food business OSI Group LLC.

TurOSI supplies processed chicken meat to supermarkets, quick service restaurants, and wholesale customers. TurOSI’s farming and processing facilities are located in Geelong, and Thomastown, Victoria. TurOSI have two secondary processing facilities in Broadmeadows, Victoria and Eagle Farm, Queensland.

Cordina is a chicken meat processor based in New South Wales. Cordina is owned by members of the Cordina family and by funds managed and controlled by PAG, a private equity firm.

Cordina supplies processed chicken meat to supermarkets, quick service restaurants, and wholesale customers. Cordina's farming and processing facilities are located in Girraween, New South Wales, with a further processing facility at Wyong, New South Wales.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third partes, and publicly
available information, including the ACCC’s Perishable Agricultural
Goods Inquiry report 2020 and previous merger matters.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
The ACCC considers that TurOSI and Cordina are not presently close
competitors in the wholesale supply of processed chicken meat.
Each Party primarily supplies processed chicken meat in the state
within which its processing facilities are located (Victoria for TurOSI
and New South Wales for Cordina), with supply outside of their
respective states being relatively limited. The ACCC recognises that
freight costs and perishability are important in the supply of
processed chicken meat and may limit interstate supply and
competition.
The ACCC considered customer feedback and tender data which
indicated the Parties currently do not closely compete in tender
opportunities to supply processed chicken meat to quick service
restaurants and wholesale customers.
Post-Acquisition, TurOSI would continue to face competition from
alternative suppliers, including the large suppliers, Baiada and
Ingham’s, which supply processed chicken across eastern Australia,
as well as regional processors operating in Australia’s eastern
states.
TurOSI and Cordina each also acquire broiler growing services,
which involve rearing day-old chicks into processing-ready chickens
grown for the purpose of chicken meat consumption. However,
competition between the Parties for growing services is limited due
to the lack of regional overlap between TurOSI’s farming and
processing operations in Victoria and Cordina’s in New South Wales.
The ACCC notes that some third parties raised concerns regarding
chicken processors’ contractual terms and potential changes to
operating policies post-Acquisition. However, the concerns raised
did not relate to the likely competitive effects of the Acquisition.
